knowledge:
- key_parameters: method=The grouping method to use ("nogroups", "apriori", "cluster", "loading", or "global") ;; groups=A list of column index vectors defining manual groups of quality measures (required for method="apriori") ;; k=The number of clusters/groups to form (required for method="cluster" and method="loading") ;; pc=The number of principal components to retain from the robust PCA (required for method="loading" and method="global")
- alternatives: affyPLM=Mentioned for detailed probe-level microarray quality assessment (e.g., PLM weights, pseudo-images, MA-plots) ;; Huber et al. (2002) PCA=Alternative PCA methods to reduce dimensionality when the number of variables exceeds the number of observations and robust PCA cannot be directly computed
- when_to_use: Use when you have a multivariate quality control report (e.g., from Affymetrix GeneChips or other platforms) for a set of arrays and want to statistically identify outlying, low-quality arrays while accounting for correlation among QC metrics.
- pitfalls: p >= n constraint=MDQC can only be used if the number of observations (arrays, n) is greater than or equal to the number of quality measures in any group (p). If p > n, you must group the variables or use PCA to reduce dimensionality ;; Small sample sizes=Caution should be taken with small datasets, as robust estimators of location and covariance may not scale properly, reducing the method's performance.

workflows.name: multivariate_qc_assessment
workflows.intent: Perform multivariate quality control assessment on microarray QC reports using Mahalanobis Distance to identify and diagnose outlying arrays.
input: allQC.csv (A user-provided data frame or matrix of quality control measures where rows represent arrays and columns represent QC metrics)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the package and the QC report data ;; 2. Run MDQC using the desired grouping or dimensionality reduction method (e.g., "nogroups", "apriori", "cluster", "loading", or "global") ;; 3. Plot the Mahalanobis distances against Chi-Squared distribution cutoffs to visually identify outliers ;; 4. Print and summarize the MDQC output to list flagged arrays exceeding the 90%, 95%, and 99% thresholds
workflows.code:
library(mdqc)
data(allQC)
dim(allQC)
allQC[1:2,]
mdout <- mdqc(allQC, method="nogroups") 
plot(mdout) 
print(mdout)
summary(mdout)
mdout <- mdqc(allQC, method="apriori",
              groups=list(1:5, 6:9, 10:11))
plot(mdout) 
mdout <- mdqc(allQC, method="cluster", k=3)
plot(mdout) 
print(mdout)
mdout <- mdqc(allQC, method="loading", k=3, pc=4)
plot(mdout)
print(mdout)
mdout <- mdqc(allQC, method="global", pc=4)
plot(mdout)
